After analyzing the Markov-style dynamics of the three-piston platform, a ball’s chance of eventual piston ejection depends only on the platform position where it first appears:
• position 1: 1⁄3
• position 2: 5⁄9
• position 3: 17⁄27

Thus a ball is likeliest to win if it first shows up in position 3.  Ball 3 begins there with certainty, whereas every later ball lands in position 3 with probability < 1, giving it a lower overall win chance.  Calculations for balls 1–6 confirm the peak at ball 3 (P₃ = 17⁄27 ≈ 0.63, greater than all others).  Hence selecting ball 3 maximizes the probability of being ejected and winning.
A ball’s eventual fate depends only on the first platform position it occupies.

Probabilities once a ball is on the platform:
• If it is in position 1: it is immediately hit with probability 1⁄3 (otherwise it rolls away forever).  P₁ = 1⁄3.
• If it is in position 2: in the next shot it is hit with probability 1⁄3, otherwise (probability 2⁄3) it shifts to position 1 and then has the previous 1⁄3 chance.  P₂ = 1⁄3 + (2⁄3)(1⁄3)=5⁄9.
• If it is in position 3: in the next shot it is hit with probability 1⁄3; with probability 1⁄3 it shifts to position 2 and with probability 1⁄3 to position 1, after which the above chances apply.  P₃ = 1⁄3 + (1⁄3)(5⁄9) + (1⁄3)(1⁄3)=17⁄27≈0.63.

Ball 1 starts in position 1, ball 2 in position 2, ball 3 in position 3. Every later ball enters the platform in position 2 or 3 with some chance, never with certainty of position 3. Therefore no ball can have a higher success probability than a ball guaranteed to start in position 3, namely ball 3.

Thus the maximum win probability is obtained by picking ball 3.
